production.note: US model years 1971-1974 (the task's US years; no opened page states US model years). Build dates: Drives.today says the V12 launched in March 1971 and 'the final E-type would be produced in September 1974'. Classic & Sports Car's panel prints build dates '1970 to 1975' for the Series III (csc-etype-s3).

body.note: Open Two Seater (roadster) and 2+2 fixed-head coupe, both on the 2+2 wheelbase; the open car has a fixed-roof sibling, so it is 'Convertible'. Drives.today gives Series 3 roadster production separately ('7982 E-type Series 3 roadsters').

displacementL.note: 5,343 cc ('5343cc (V12 OC)'). Supercars.net gives the same '5343 cc / 326.0 in3' (supercars-etype-s3-2plus2).

aspiration.note: Carburetted, no forced induction: 'With four Zenith-Strombergs it was rated 272bhp'.

transmission.note: '4-Speed Manual or Optional 3-Speed Auto'. Drives.today names the automatic as 'the Borg-Warner 12J three speed auto, not the four speed manual' (drives-today-etype-s3).

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (enthusiast and non-major publication sources). Jaguar's US launch rating, recorded as published, following the convention that pre-1980 US cars were rated in SAE gross. Quote (Drives.today): a claimed output of '314bhp SAE' at the March 1971 launch, and 'the DIN power figure was more like 272bhp'. Supercars.net's panel: '234.1 kw / 314 bhp @ 6200 rpm' (supercars-etype-s3-2plus2, same figures on supercars-etype-s3-roadster). Classic & Sports Car gives the European rating: 'With four Zenith-Strombergs it was rated 272bhp' (csc-etype-s3). Later US-market cars were rated lower under SAE net, but no opened page gave those figures.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (weak sources; body attribution inconsistent). Quote (Supercars.net, 1971 Series III 2+2 panel): '1533 kg / 3380 lbs'. Unique Cars and Parts prints the same number for the open car: 'Roadster: 3,380 lbs.' with a 'DHC' at 3,361 lbs (uniquecars-etype-s3). The two agree on 3,380 lb, and both present it as a kerb figure (Supercars.net's panel labels it 'curb weight'; Unique Cars and Parts lists it under kerb weights), but they attribute it to different bodies (2+2 vs Roadster) and neither ties it to the US market.

sources.title: We tell the story of the Jaguar E-type Series 3
1971 Jaguar E-Type Series III Roadster (Nick Dellis)

discrepancies.reason: Rating standards: 314 bhp was Jaguar's SAE gross launch claim for the US; 272 bhp is the European (DIN) rating; Unique Cars and Parts prints '276 bhp (206 kW) @ 5850 rpm' without naming a standard.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 314 hp, the US-market SAE gross launch rating, per the classic-car rule; the DIN figure is described in the power note.

discrepancies.reason: Supercars.net gives 3,380 lb for the 2+2 and the roadster alike; Unique Cars and Parts gives 3,380 lb for the roadster and 3,361 lb for a 'DHC'. The bodies the figures belong to are inconsistent between sources.

reviewNotes: Weight: both opened sources print 3,380 lb as a kerb figure but attribute it to different bodies (2+2 vs Roadster), and neither ties it to the US market. Power is the SAE gross launch claim; the 1972-1974 US SAE net ratings were not found on an opened page. A period US road-test spec panel or a Jaguar US brochure for 1971-74 should replace both figures.
provisionalNote: Power (314 hp SAE gross) rests on Drives.today (no named author) and Supercars.net (enthusiast), agreeing. Weight (3,380 lb) rests on Supercars.net and Unique Cars and Parts (both enthusiast-grade), agreeing on the number but not on which body it describes. A Jaguar US brochure or a major magazine's 1971-74 spec panel would replace both. Production is also weak: the 1971-1974 range rests on build dates (March 1971 to September 1974; Classic & Sports Car prints 1970 to 1975), and no opened page states US model years.
